Agent Name: Planner
Step Number: 1
Reason for Mistake: The Planner misinterpreted the core objective of the investigation by incorrectly prioritizing measurement sensitivity (precision of volume change) over the fundamental definition of "rate of evaporation" in a standard educational context. The agent assumed that because a balance might not detect the *mass* of a single drop, it is therefore unsuitable for measuring the *rate* (mass loss over time). This is a logical fallacy; a balance is the standard instrument for measuring evaporation rates because evaporation is defined as a loss of mass, and balances are designed to measure mass changes over time intervals, regardless of the small magnitude of individual drops. By focusing on the inability to measure a single drop rather than the ability to measure the cumulative loss over time, the Planner selected the meter stick (which measures length/volume) instead of the balance, leading to the wrong answer.
